topic.readerProblem: A marketer sees HubSpot's free AEO Grader score and wants to know what it measures, what it cannot tell them about being recommended by AI, and whether to use it or pay for something else.
topic.connection: AEOeye audits whether AI engines name a brand when buyers ask; the page explains where a brand-perception grade stops and a buyer-question audit starts, with honest pointers to monitoring tools.

assessment: The page is a documentation-based guide to HubSpot's AEO Grader (now titled AI Search Grader): engines, five scored dimensions with their published weights, data sources, price of the related HubSpot AEO product, and the limits of a one-time brand grade. It rests on HubSpot's own pages fetched on 2026-10-03, SparkToro's run-variance study, OpenAI's crawler documentation, an arXiv paper and AEOeye's audit records with their caveat. It does not claim hands-on use, does not reproduce a report, and does not judge the product's accuracy.

sources.supports: Free one-time check, no account, results under two minutes; engines GPT-5.4 mini, Perplexity, Gemini; five dimensions with 40/20/20/10/10 weights; accepts any brand; inputs; page is titled AI Search Grader and hubspot.com/aeo-grader redirects to it.

HubSpot AEO $50/month ($45 annual), 25 prompts, ChatGPT/Gemini/Perplexity, free 25-prompt trial, beta label, included in Marketing Hub Pro/Enterprise; FAQ says the Grader runs pre-set queries and ChatGPT and Gemini pull from training data while Perplexity uses live search.
AI Search Sensor is a free industry-level dashboard that won't show your brand's visibility.
600 volunteers, 12 prompts, 2,961 runs; under 1-in-100 chance ChatGPT or Google's AI gives the same brand list in any two responses.
OAI-SearchBot surfaces websites in ChatGPT's search features; GPTBot is for model training; settings are independent.
Abstract: AI search shows a systematic and overwhelming bias towards earned media over brand-owned and social content.
GEO is also known as answer engine optimization (AEO).
